message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in code generation tasks. However,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">repository-level code generation</jats:italic>
                    presents unique challenges, particularly due to the need to utilize information spread across multiple files within a repository. Specifically, successful generation depends on a solid grasp of both general, context-agnostic knowledge and specific, context-dependent knowledge. While LLMs are widely used for the context-agnostic aspect, existing retrieval-based approaches sometimes fall short as they are limited in obtaining a broader and deeper repository context. In this article, we present
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">
                      <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    </jats:italic>
                    , a novel code generation framework designed for statically typed programming languages.
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    enhances repository-level code generation by integrating relevant
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">c</jats:italic>
                    ode
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">a</jats:italic>
                    nd
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">t</jats:italic>
                    ype context. Specifically, it leverages static analyzers to extract type dependencies and merges this information with retrieved code to create comprehensive prompts for LLMs. To evaluate the effectiveness of
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    , we adapt and construct benchmarks that include 199 Java tasks and 90 Rust tasks. The results show that
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    outperforms the RepoCoder baseline by up to 14.44% and 17.35%, in terms of compile@
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\( k \)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and pass@
                    <jats:inline-formula content-type="math/tex">
                      <jats:tex-math notation="LaTeX" version="MathJax">\( k \)</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    scores. In addition, the generalizability of
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    is assessed using various LLMs, including both code-specialized models and general-purpose models. Our findings indicate consistent performance improvements across all models, which underlines the practicality of
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    . Furthermore, we evaluate the time consumption of
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    in a large open source repository, and the results demonstrate the scalability of
                    <jats:sc>CatCoder</jats:sc>
                    .
                  </jats:p>
title:
<scp>CatCoder</scp>
                    : Repository-Level Code Generation with Relevant Code and Type Context
